Tooltip_Fletcher_HipQuiver: Worn on the right hip. Holds only arrows and bolts; nocking or cocking from it is faster.
Tooltip_Fletcher_NoiseArrow: A rattling can on a blunt arrow. Wherever it lands it makes a racket for a few seconds that draws zombies within about 18 tiles: shoot it away from you to pull a crowd off your path. Barely hurts.
Tooltip_Fletcher_FireArrow: A fuel-soaked rag behind the point. Carry a lighter or matches and it is lit as you loose it: it sets alight whatever it hits, or starts a fire where it lands, and burns away. Fires spread: mind the grass and your own walls.
Tooltip_Fletcher_DamagedArrow: Bent shaft, torn fletching: it won't fly true. Re-fletch it with one Fletching to shoot it again.
Tooltip_Fletcher_DamagedBolt: Its vanes are torn: re-fletch it with one Fletching to shoot it again.
Tooltip_Fletcher_ArcheryTarget: A straw bale with a painted face. Put it down and shoot at it: arrows stick in the straw without breaking, and you learn from every hit until Archery 3.
Tooltip_Fletcher_HideGluePot: Cook it on a stove or campfire for about an hour, then pour off the glue.
Tooltip_Fletcher_HideGluePotCooked: Pour it off to get a tube of glue and your pot back.
Tooltip_Fletcher_GreenStave: Green wood. Lay it on a Stave Rack to season it (a bow stave takes 3 days, a longbow stave 5): a bow from seasoned wood hits harder, reaches farther and wears slower.
Tooltip_Fletcher_SeasonedStave: Seasoned on a stave rack: a bow made from it hits harder, reaches farther and wears slower.
Tooltip_Fletcher_BenchDesc: A fletcher's workbench with a jig and a vise: fletch arrows and bolts five at a time, faster, as matched sets that fly truer and break less.
Tooltip_Fletcher_Jig: Holds an arrow shaft while its fletching sets, so every vane sits the same. Part of a Fletcher's Bench.
Tooltip_Fletcher_Matched: One of a matched set made at a Fletcher's Bench: strays less and breaks less than an ordinary arrow.
Tooltip_Fletcher_RackDesc: A bowyer's drying rack. Lay green bow and longbow staves on its pegs to season them: 3 days for a bow stave, 5 for a longbow stave. Seasoned wood makes a stronger bow.
Tooltip_Fletcher_BackQuiver: Worn across the back, with a bow on your back or a backpack if you like. Holds only arrows and bolts, and many more than the hip quiver. Arrows come from the hip quiver first; nocking from the back quiver is a little faster than from a bag.
Tooltip_Fletcher_FishingArrow: A barbed arrow on a fishing line. Aim at fishable water and watch for fish breaking the surface: shoot one as it rises and reel it in. Missed shots are reeled back. Choose it from the reload menu.
Tooltip_Fletcher_PlasticVanes: Fletching cut from plastic. Arrows fletched with it last longer and break less, but stray a little more than feathered ones.
Tooltip_Fletcher_TapeVanes: Folded tape fletching: quick and needs no tools, but arrows fletched with it stray more and wear out fast. Not good enough for a matched set.
Tooltip_Fletcher_BoardBowStave: A bow-length strip sawn from a plank. Lumber is already dry: string it as it is.
